SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Alfred Lehmann,
native of Germany taken by me
at Hongkew Stn. on the 12-4-40. and interpreted by P.S.88 V.C. Thomson

Alfred Lehmann, 35 years of age, residing at 737/3
East Broadway. I was on 11-4-40 at Hongkew Market where I
met Miss Haas and greeted her. I know her for nearly one year.
She told me that it would not be good that Jewish Refugees
should vote for Japanese. Then I told her that I have no
voting rights and have nothing to do with the voting. I was
on my way home when suddenly one car stopped and one Japanese
pushed me into a car with a pistol in his hand and returned
with me to the Hongkew Market. When we arrived there he
ordered me out of the car and the said Japanese walked with
me upstairs to the voting place. He seemed to me that he
was looking for someone there. I took the opportunity when
he was looking around, and descended down the stairs when I
turned around the corner and proceeded by Woosung Road to
Chaufong Road, No.165, where I met Mr. Novak. I left that
place probably a little past 12 noon and went for tiffin in
Mr. Hoffmann's Restaurant on E. Seward Road No.610.
P.S. I came to Hongkew Market in a m/car. Mr. Hirsch
is the Chairman of the Voting Committee and lives at 165
Chaufong Road.

(Signed) Alfred Lehmann.

My name is Wong Siau Dee, age 31, native of Nansieng, residing at No. 128 Quinsan Road and I am employed as a chauffeur in the Shanghai Japanese Residents Association at the said address, I having been thus employed for the past two years.

Yesterday (10/4/40) I was instructed by my employers to transport Jews from Chaofoong Road near Ward Road to the Hongkew Market, Boone Road which journey I made about twenty times, having commenced the transportation at 10 a.m. and completed about 5 p.m.

About 8 a.m. to-day, I was again instructed by my employers to repeat the transportation.

About 11.20 a.m. just having turned round my car and parked same beside the market Boone Road, after having taken four Jews to the market, a Japanese male after having forced into my car a Jewess, ordered me to drive the car, which I did, driving the car along Boone Road then turned East along Seward Road.

Sitting beside me was a Jew, whom I picked up from Chaofoong Road and he remained in the car during the incident.

Whilst the car was proceeding along Seward Road the Jewess quarrelled with the Japanese all the time, both speaking in a foreign language.

On arrival at the corner of E.Seward and Chaofoong Roads the Japanese ordered me to stop the car and then told the Jew to get out of the car.

Then the Japanese again ordered me to drive the car

Made by.  P.C. 304 Scott        Forwarded by. O.B. Perkins, C.I.

Sir,

    At about 11 a.m. 11-4-40, whilst conducting traffic
at the Hongkew Market polling booth, I observed a black
closed m/car bearing licence No. 4067 draw up about 30 yards
East of the polling booth on the North side. Then a
woman whom I took to be a foreigner entered the m/car
as if in a hurry, and was followed by a Japanese male.
As the m/car was driving off, I could observe through
the rear window that they were struggling. The woman
whilst entering the m/car did not call for police
assistance. The m/car then drove East on Boone Road.
After observing the struggle in the m/car, my suspicions
were then aroused, that the occurrence might prove to
be a case of abduction. I then immediately reported
the occurrence to the Sergeant on charge Room Forty. This
was also witnessed by P.C. 11 Crouch and P.P.S.
Steinberg.

当我在文监师路与汉伯里路口的虹口市场电车

编号1037，沿文监师路由西向东从我身边驶过，并在越过
汉伯里路路口约五十码处停下。

    当车停下时，我看到一名身材矮小的日本男子，
约35岁，身穿浅黄褐色夹克，灰色法兰绒
长裤，未戴帽子，戴着眼镜，他打开车门，抓住并扭转
一名中等身材的外国妇女的手臂，该妇女身穿长款大衣，
配有浅色毛皮领子，并强行将她推入

Strange
Attack On
Woman

Miss C. Haas Kidnapped
In Hongkew, Beaten
And Then Released

Miss Cecilia Haas, Czechoslovakian, was kidnapped on Boone Road, outside the Hongkew Market, by a Japanese in plainclothes yesterday morning, driven off towards Yangtzepoo, badly beaten about the face, head and body and then released yesterday afternoon.

Shanghai Municipal Police and Japanese authorities were last night making inquiries into the brutal attack on the foreign woman, which is believed to have been carried out probably by an unbalanced Japanese, who is now being sought by the authorities.

Miss Haas, who resides in the Embankment Building, was standing on Boone Road, outside the Hongkew Market, talking with some Jewish emigrants, at about 10.45 a.m. when suddenly a car drove up to the sidewalk, a Japanese jumped out, pushed her inside and the car, with a Chinese chauffeur, at the wheel drove off immediately.

An alarm was immediately raised and officers of the Hongkew Police Station were informed. All efforts to trace the car, licence 4067, in which Miss Haas was kidnapped, failed.

**Brought To Consulate**

At 2.45 p.m. Miss Haas was taken to the Japanese Consulate-General by some Japanese. She displayed signs of brutal attack on her head, face and arms and immediately proceeded to the General Hospital for treatment. Later she returned to her apartment in the Embankment Building.

She related that she was driven off towards Yangtzepoo and despite the fact that she struggled, she could not free herself. She was badly beaten and finally allowed to go by her captor.

It was alleged, but not confirmed yesterday, that Miss Haas was suspected by the Japanese who kidnapped her, of attempting to influence votes of emigres north of the creek.

**Japanese Withheld Comment**

Japanese authorities here last night withheld all comment on the reported abduction of Miss Cecilia Haas, a citizen of former Czechoslovakia, allegedly by Japanese, pending the clarification of the case which was understood to be under investigation by the Hongkew Station of the Shanghai Municipal Police.

Motorcar, Licence No. 4076, which was alleged to have been used in the reported abduction was halted by Municipal Police near the Garden Bridge in the afternoon. Its Chinese chauffeur was taken to Hongkew Station for questioning.

Miss Haas, it was learned, was picked up about noon in the suburbs of Shanghai beyond Yangtzepoo by a passing Japanese truck, whose driver brought her to the headquarters of the Japanese Consular Police at Boone and Nanzing Roads, where she was understood to have made a statement. She subsequently went to the General Hospital to be treated for bruises and lacerations.

FILE

离奇
袭击
妇女

C. 哈斯小姐在虹口遭绑架、殴打
随后获释

捷克斯洛伐克籍的塞西莉亚·哈斯（Cecilia Haas）小姐于昨天上午在虹口市场外的文监师路（Boone Road）被一名便衣日本人绑架，被驱往杨树浦方向，面部、头部和身体遭到严重殴打，随后于昨天下午获释。

上海公共租界工部局警务处和日本当局昨晚正在调查这起对外国妇女的野蛮袭击事件，据信这很可能是一名精神失常的日本人所为，当局目前正在搜捕此人。

哈斯小姐居住在堤岸大楼（Embankment Building），上午约 10 时 45 分，她正站在虹口市场外的文监师路上与一些犹太移民交谈，突然一辆汽车驶上人行道，一名日本人跳下车，将她推入车内，随后由一名中国司机驾驶的汽车立即驶离。

警报随即拉响，虹口巡捕房的警官接到通知。所有追踪载有哈斯小姐的被绑车辆（牌照号 4067）的努力均告失败。

**被带至领事馆**

下午 2 时 45 分，哈斯小姐被几名日本人带至日本总领事馆。她的头部、面部和手臂显示出遭受野蛮袭击的痕迹，随后立即前往广慈医院（General Hospital）接受治疗。之后她返回了堤岸大楼的公寓。

她叙述称，她被驱往杨树浦方向，尽管她奋力挣扎，但无法脱身。她遭到严重殴打，最终被绑架者放行。

据称（但昨日未获证实），绑架哈斯小姐的日本人怀疑她试图影响苏州河以北移民的投票。

**日方不予置评**

驻沪日本当局昨晚对前捷克斯洛伐克公民塞西莉亚·哈斯小姐据称被日本人绑架一事拒绝发表任何评论，以待案情澄清，据悉上海公共租界工部局警务处虹口巡捕房正在对此进行调查。

据称用于实施上述绑架的汽车（牌照号 4076）于下午被工部局警务处在花园桥附近拦下。其中国司机被带至虹口巡捕房接受讯问。

据悉，哈斯小姐于中午左右在上海郊区杨树浦以外被一辆过路的日本卡车拾起，司机将她带到位于文监师路和南京路交叉口的日本领事警察总部，据悉她在那里作了陈述。随后她前往广慈医院治疗挫伤和裂伤。

归档

pages.en:
Foreign Woman
Manhandled

Japanese Uses Pistol
Butt to Injure Miss
Cecilia Haas

With bruises on her arms and legs
and a serious injury to an eye, pre-
sumably caused by the butt of a pistol
with which she was struck during her
four-hour captivity, Miss Cecilia Haas,
Czechoslovakian, was nursing her
wounds in her Embankment Building
apartment last night and was unable
to speak to a "North-China Daily
News" reporter.

Investigations revealed that Miss
Haas, who is connected with the
catering department of Jewish re-
fugees living at the Embankment
Building, was standing on Boone
Road near the Hongkew Market at
about 11.15 a.m. yesterday when a
car, licence No. 4607, drove up to
her, a Japanese ordered her to sit
down in the rear, and the vehicle
finally drove off in the direction of
Yangtzepoo. Shrieking and attempt-
ing to free herself, Miss Haas was
seen being finally overpowered by
the Japanese and a foreigner who
were sitting on either side of her
while a Chinese chauffeur was
driving.

Questioned at H.Q.

The car proceeded to a piece of
vacant ground on Ward Road where
a truck-load of Japanese gendarmerie
saw her being forcefully taken from
the car. The gendarmes intervened
and accompanied her to their head-
quarters where he was questioned.
When permitted to leave, Miss
Haas, proceeded to the Japanese
Consulate-General where she reported
the matter and then went to the Gen-
eral Hospital where her wounds were
treated.

The car used in the kidnapping was
learned by the "North-China Daily
News" to be registered in the name
of the Japanese Residents' Corpora-
tion. It was found abandoned at the
intersection of Seward Road and
Broadway at 2.30 p.m. yesterday and
was subsequently taken to Hongkew
police station.

It was generally believed that the
Japanese suspected Miss Haas of
urging Jewish refugees not to vote
for the Japanese candidates in the
municipal elections. Close friends of
the victim of yesterday's cowardly
attack assured the "North-China Daily
News" that Miss Haas had never at
any time discussed the elections with
anyone. Interesting side-light on the
case, is the fact that eye-witnesses to
the kidnapping told the "North-China
Daily News" reporter that a foreign-
er, appearing to be a Jewish refugee,
was in the car with the Japanese who
forced Miss Haas to drive away with
them.

FILED

外籍妇女
遭粗暴对待

日本人使用手枪枪托
致塞西莉亚·哈斯小姐受伤

手臂和腿部有淤青，眼部受重伤（据推测是在四小时拘禁期间被手枪枪托击打所致），捷克斯洛伐克籍的塞西莉亚·哈斯小姐昨晚在其堤岸大楼的公寓中养伤，无法接受《字林西报》记者的采访。

调查显示，哈斯小姐与居住在堤岸大楼的犹太难民的餐饮部门有关联，昨天上午约 11 时 15 分，她正站在虹口市场附近的文监师路上，此时一辆牌照号为 4607 的汽车驶到她面前，一名日本人命令她坐在后座，随后车辆最终向杨树浦方向驶去。目击者看到，哈斯小姐尖叫并试图挣脱，但最终被坐在她两侧的一名日本人和一名外国人制服，当时由一名中国司机驾驶。

在总部受询

该车驶至华德路（Ward Road）的一块空地，一卡车日本宪兵看到她被强行从车上带下。宪兵介入并陪同她前往他们的总部，她在那里接受了讯问。获准离开后，哈斯小姐前往日本总领事馆报告此事，然后去了广慈医院治疗伤口。

《字林西报》获悉，用于绑架的汽车注册在日本居留民团名下。该车于昨天下午 2 时 30 分被发现弃置于西华德路（Seward Road）和百老汇路的交叉口，随后被送往虹口巡捕房。

人们普遍认为，日本人怀疑哈斯小姐鼓动犹太难民在市政选举中不投票给日本候选人。这位昨日懦弱袭击受害者的密友向《字林西报》保证，哈斯小姐从未与任何人讨论过选举问题。此案的一个有趣旁证是，绑架案的目击者告诉《字林西报》记者，车内除日本人外，还有一名看似为犹太难民的外国人，他们强迫哈斯小姐随车离去。

归档

pages.en:
APP 1 2 1940

Czech Woman
Returns Home
Beaten, Bruised

Miss Cecilia Haas, Czech national who was kidnapped on Boone Road near the Hongkew Market polling booths yesterday morning allegedly by two Japanese plainclothes men in an automobile was returned to her home in the Embankment Building late in the afternoon badly beaten, and bruised.

An ardent advocate of retaining the British and American majority on the S.M.C., Miss Haas had taken active part in the two-day election by carrying voters to the polls and proselytising among the Jewish refugees of Hongkew, according to neighbors, interviewed by THE CHINA PRESS.

It was believed yesterday that she had been attempting to show refugees with whom she was conversing near the polls, that voting for the British and American candidates would be best when the car which had been standing nearby pulled up to the curb and she was forcibly dragged into the back seat by two men while a third behind the wheel turned the vehicle toward Yangtzepoo. The hour was 10:45.

Screaming Woman

A car was later spied by witnesses speeding along Ward Road with a screaming woman in the back.

Miss Haas returned to her home about 4 p.m., in a dishevelled condition with her eyes badly blackened and her legs badly bruised. There were teeth marks on her cheeks where she had been bitten by one of her savage captors. Shortly after arriving home she gave full details to police and later visited a doctor.

Earlier yesterday morning another woman was the victim of the Japanese directed "Ta Tao" police force in a different section of town.

Mrs. E. L. Dean, wife of a Butterfield and Swire official living at 43b Edinburgh Road, slightly damaged a bicycle while driving along Yu Yuen Road at 9:45 o'clock. She was stopped by "Ta Tao" men who asked her to accompany them to a "Ta Tao" station although they had no authority to do so in the district.

Refuses To Comply

Instead of following instructions the frightened woman drove to a nearby British military post where she was afforded protection.

At this time a liaison officer of British Military Headquarters arrived on the scene. He immediately phoned to Bubbling Well police station and to the Japanese gendarmerie at Jessfield Road.

When the S.M.P. arrived they decided Mrs. Dean should report the accident at Bubbling Well although it was an insignificant case. Accordingly she was about to drive off when the "Ta Tao" police refused to permit her departure and surrounded the car notwithstanding the presence of S.M.P. and British tommyes. A bad situation was saved when a senior officer of the "Ta Tao" arrived in answer to the British officer's call. He ordered his men away from the car which Mrs. Dean promptly drove to Bubbling Well station.

（印：FILE）

APP 1 2 1940

捷克妇女
回家
遍体鳞伤

捷克斯洛伐克籍的塞西莉亚·哈斯小姐，昨天上午在虹口市场投票站附近的文监师路据称被两名便衣日本人乘汽车绑架，于傍晚时分回到其在堤岸大楼的家中，身上多处遭殴打和淤青。

据《大美晚报》（THE CHINA PRESS）采访的邻居称，哈斯小姐是保留工部局董事会中英美多数席位的热烈倡导者，她通过将选民送往投票站以及在虹口犹太难民中进行游说，积极参与了为期两天的选举。

昨日据信，当她正试图向在投票站附近与她交谈的难民表明，投票给英美候选人最为有利时，停在附近的一辆汽车靠边停下，她被两名男子强行拖入后座，而第三名男子则在驾驶位上将车驶向杨树浦。当时时间为 10 时 45 分。

尖叫的妇女

后来有目击者发现一辆汽车沿华德路飞驰，后座有一名妇女在尖叫。

哈斯小姐于下午 4 时左右回到家，衣衫凌乱，双眼严重青肿，腿部严重淤青。她的脸颊上有牙印，是被其中一名野蛮的绑架者咬伤的。回家后不久，她向警方提供了详细情况，随后去看医生。

昨天清晨早些时候，另一名妇女在城市的不同区域成为日本指使的“大道”（Ta Tao）警察部队的受害者。

E. L. 迪恩（Dean）夫人是怡和洋行（Butterfield and Swire）一名官员的妻子，居住在爱丁堡路 43b 号。9 时 45 分，她驾车沿愚园路行驶时轻微损坏了一辆自行车。她被“大道”人员拦下，要求他们陪同前往“大道”警局，尽管他们在该地区无权这样做。

拒绝服从

这名受惊的妇女没有听从指令，而是驾车前往附近的英军哨所，在那里得到了保护。

此时，英军司令部的联络官抵达现场。他立即致电静安寺巡捕房和极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）的日本宪兵队。

当工部局警务处人员到达时，他们决定迪恩夫人应去静安寺巡捕房报告事故，尽管这是一起微不足道的案件。因此，当她准备驾车离开时，“大道”警察拒绝让她离开，并包围了汽车，尽管工部局警务处人员和英国士兵在场。随着一名“大道”高级军官响应英国军官的呼叫赶到，糟糕的局面得以化解。他命令手下离开汽车，迪恩夫人随即驾车前往静安寺巡捕房。
